about: Tolerances for X_ITE on the add-on's X3D vs X_ITE on Blender's own glb, per frozen scene: measured mean |delta| x 1.5 + 2, written before the gate was used (calibration run).

vertex_colours.why: Confirmed: the add-on writes the 'Col' colour attribute as ColorRGBA and X_ITE multiplies it in; Blender's glTF exporter (default export_vertex_color MATERIAL) leaves it out because no material node reads it, so the glb cube is plain grey, as Blender itself renders it. Which one is right is a mapping-table question (mesh:colour_attribute is 'carried').

hierarchy.why: Same as cameras: two cubes with no material.

four_lights.why: Confirmed: the area light is written by the add-on as a DirectionalLight (receipt: approximated) and left out of the glb (glTF has no area light); point and spot intensities differ in units (add-on X_ITE light units vs COMPAT W/4pi candela).

cameras.why: Confirmed: an object with no material. The add-on writes Blender's default look (PhysicalMaterial 0.8 grey, roughness 0.5); the glb has no material, so X_ITE uses glTF's default (white, metallic 1, roughness 1).

smooth_torus.why: Suspected: smooth-shading normals: the add-on writes per-corner normals, the glb per-vertex; edges differ by a few levels.

keyframes.why: Same as cameras: a cube with no material (frame 1 of the animation).

emissive_glass.why: Within 0.12 where drawn: emission and alpha blending agree.

loose_edges.why: Confirmed: Blender's glTF exporter omits a mesh of loose edges only ('has no primitives and will be omitted'); the add-on writes an IndexedLineSet, so only the add-on's frame shows the hexagon.

rig: 512 x 512 headless Chromium 157.0.8103.78 (Playwright's, SwiftShader), X_ITE 16.7.1, judge Viewpoint from same_renderer.judge_view
